title: Jalayirid Sultanate
capsule: The Jalayirid Sultanate emerged from the wreckage of the Ilkhanate after Abu Sa'id Bahadur Khan's death in 1335, when the Jalayir — a Turkicized Mongol tribe — seized Baghdad and the southwest Iranian plateau under Hasan Buzurg (r. 1336–1356). The realm reached its apex under Shaykh Uways (r. 1356–1374), who extended control from Baghdad through Azerbaijan into the Caucasus and became a major patron of Persian arts, bridging Ilkhanid and Timurid artistic traditions. Sultan Ahmad Jalayir (r. 1382–1410) ruled intermittently as the sultanate was squeezed between Timurid invasions from the east and the Qara Qoyunlu Turkmen from the northwest; Ahmad was killed by Qara Yusuf in 1410. The last Jalayirid ruler, Husayn II, was killed in 1431, bringing the dynasty to extinction.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political core (Iraq and western Iran) is well documented in Persian chronicles, but exact frontier zones in the Caucasus and eastern Anatolia fluctuated and are imprecisely mapped.
